legend.partly: done in part or by a fallback

rules.rule: The engine's raw output is written once and never rewritten.
rules.why: Every page, count and card is derived from it; if it changes, nothing can be checked later.
rules.where: lesson_pipeline.process writes scribe.json once; understanding.json is regenerated from it

rules.rule: Transcribe the whole lesson track, never 25-second chunks.
rules.why: Same engine on 25-s chunks lost 3 of 8 of Medi's mistakes (audit 2026-09-05).

rules.rule: No vocabulary list in the recognizer's ear on the primary pass.
rules.why: A prompted engine inserted Buset, Ya3ni and a whole chat sentence that nobody said.
rules.where: transcribe(): no keyterms; vocabulary is used only after recognition

rules.rule: An unknown form stays unknown and flagged; it is never replaced by the nearest Doc word.
rules.why: Medi's 'sameeh' for 'mneeh' is the lesson; a silent fix erases it.
rules.where: arabizi.Matcher tiers exact > loose > skeleton; fuzzy only for chat-anchored words

rules.rule: Every reported miss or moment carries its audio clip.
rules.why: Nobody, human or machine, is trusted without the sound.

rules.rule: Hash the audio and the raw transcript and keep a second copy.
rules.why: Today the raw file lives on one PC only.

rules.rule: Speaker = recording channel, never a guess.
rules.why: On the mixed Meet audio the engine put nearly every word on one speaker.
rules.where: planned: two named tracks (Ennuicastr / Craig); today: pitch fallback with a 15 % unlabeled floor, shown on the page

rules.rule: 'More Arabic = Amal' is a hint, never a fact.
rules.why: Medi's Arabic share grows every lesson; the rule flips.
rules.where: lesson_pipeline.label_speakers is only used when the engine already split two voices

rules.rule: When speakers are unclear, per-speaker numbers show '–' with the reason.
rules.why: A wrong number is worse than no number.

rules.rule: A miss needs a signal: Amal corrects or recasts, or Medi asks or says he forgot. Medi's spelling alone is never a miss.
rules.why: ASR auto-corrects learners (LearnerVoice finding, confirmed on our audio).

rules.rule: A grammar slip (article, gender, tense, plural) keeps the word out of 'missed'.
rules.why: The word is known; the slip is scored separately.

rules.rule: Glue words (shu, bas, ya3ni, tamam …) are never graded.
rules.why: They are conversation moves, not vocabulary.

rules.rule: Keep the stumble: false starts, repeats, 'nitla' for ne6la3. Never clean them.
rules.why: They are the evidence Anees exists for.
rules.where: engine choice (Scribe full track); planned: golden clips 9, 17, 18, 19 fail the build if a new engine version cleans them

rules.rule: 'Possible miss' stays labelled possible until Amal taps.
rules.why: The reaction detector is about 50 % precise.
rules.where: report wording; after-link verdicts re-score the event

rules.rule: 'New' is inferred from the lesson, then confirmed by the Doc: a word Amal introduces (explains, spells, types) that is not in the Doc snapshot taken before the lesson = new (inferred); when it appears in the Doc afterwards = new (confirmed). Never a lesson-count heuristic.
rules.why: Medi 2026-09-05: new words are not on the master list yet during the lesson and appear afterwards; the lesson itself shows whether he is learning or reviewing.
rules.where: buckets.compute: new only if Amal typed the word/family in that lesson's chat or Medi asked for it, heard in that one lesson only, not drilled (built 2026-09-05: 7 new words for Sep 4, not 154). The 'not in the Doc before the lesson' check waits for the live Doc import (publish-to-web URL).

rules.rule: The Google Doc is the only word truth. The app never writes it.
rules.why: Amal owns the list.

rules.rule: A Doc lemma covers its conjugations: Basa6tek belongs to babse6's family.
rules.why: 16 of Amal's 21 typed Sep-4 forms are conjugations the Doc does not list.
rules.where: understand_lesson.family_key (consonant skeleton); planned: first-tier, and split multi-word entries so ne6la3 is a target

rules.rule: New words never mix with missed words in practice; strict review first.
rules.why: Different loops.

rules.rule: Code never contacts Amal. Links are minted; Medi sends them.
rules.why: Her time and trust.

rules.rule: Amal's tap beats any machine label.
rules.why: She is the ground truth.

rules.rule: At most 5 questions, clips of at most 15 s, one tap each; target 3 to 5 minutes; measure it.
rules.why: Her budget is minutes.
rules.where: after_questions.py; timing measured only on stand-ins so far

rules.rule: Lessons are public by choice: audio, clips and transcripts stay on the open site; any transcription provider may receive the audio.
rules.why: Medi 2026-09-05: nothing sensitive is said. Amal said yes to all of it the same day (relayed by Medi).
rules.where: docs/ pages are public; no consent gate in code

rules.rule: No guessed number. Unknown shows '–' and why.
rules.why: Medi's standing rule.

rules.rule: Counts are counts. 'Better' or 'accurate' only with a named metric and human labels.
rules.why: No word-perfect transcript exists yet.
rules.where: engine report wording; AI reports cards

rules.rule: Nothing is emailed before the page is pushed and answers 200.
rules.why: A link to a 404 is a lie.

rules.rule: Paid calls stop at 90 % of the budget.
rules.why: Ceiling prices, no surprises.

rules.rule: Freeze clips, hashes and test arms before any output is seen.
rules.why: So a result cannot be steered.
rules.where: Codex bake-offs; Claude audit reproduced 65/65 hashes

rules.rule: An engine is replaced only on held-out, Amal-labelled events, tested on full tracks.
rules.why: 20 clips of one verb from one lesson prove direction, not superiority.

tabs.system: System rules: the mechanics (recording, transcribing, who spoke, publishing, numbers, research method)
tabs.words: Word and grammar rules: what counts as a mistake, what is new, what Amal decides
